objective: Build goal-oriented, adjoint-weighted discretization error estimates as a mission primitive alongside the existing grid-refinement channel, prototype them where the refinement answer is known, and demonstrate them on a case whose adjoint gradient is already verified against finite differences
rationale: The refinement channel is in house, mature, and refuses to answer on most of the lab's ladders, which is exactly the gap a goal-oriented estimate fills. The existing implementation carries both the grid-convergence index and the least-squares scatter-aware fit with a shared set of asymptotic guards, and it returns nothing unless the ladder earned it, a guard added after sealed certificates printed a band under a caption they had not earned. The measured consequence is that refusal is the normal case: all five two-dimensional ladders refitted at both dimension conventions earn no band, one large ladder is monotone with an observed order of 2.253 inside the window and still not conclusive because its extrapolation lands 24 percent above the highest rung, another ladder returns an observed order above 10, another above 7 and clamped, and a valve case returns three different observed orders from three triplets with grid uncertainty landing near 20 percent rather than the 1.4 percent one triplet suggested. Meanwhile a repo-wide search for goal-oriented or adjoint-weighted estimation returns exactly one hit and it is the strategy line asking for it. The reason to build it now rather than earlier is that the missing ingredient arrived: the adjoint on the transonic wing rung is bit-reproducible across three independent runs at the same iteration count and its gradient is verified against finite differences, with the two evaluable components landing at 0.18 and 0.93 percent, so the dual solution the estimate weights by is a trusted object on at least one case rather than a hope. The prototype belongs where the truth is known, on the geometric flat-plate ladder whose refinement ratio is exactly two per step across five levels, so the goal-oriented estimate can be graded against the refinement channel's answer instead of being graded against itself. Axis A: reading-kind, priced from two measured bases. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0.

cost_basis: measured on two bases, both named: the flat-plate coefficient study spent 44.7 core-min for 42 solves at the 13,056-cell level restarting from a converged baseline, so about 1.06 core-min per solve there, and the transonic wing adjoint at the reopened rung cost 7.33 core-min at 368 iterations; the prototype needs a handful of flat-plate residual evaluations on a refined space plus one wing adjoint already on disk and one confirming primal, which comes to about 45 core-min at the same rank counts
expected_knowledge_gain: Three outcomes that separate, and each changes what the lab reports. One: the goal-oriented estimate agrees with the refinement channel where the refinement channel earns a band, and returns a number where it refuses, which makes it the primitive the strategy asks for and gives the refusing ladders an answer for the first time. Two: it agrees where the ladder is clean and disagrees where the ladder is noisy, which is the interesting case and means the two channels are measuring different things and must be reported side by side rather than combined. Three: it disagrees on the clean ladder, which falsifies the implementation and is caught by the cheapest possible control rather than by a customer. The per-cell error contribution to the objective is a by-product either way and is the input an adaptive refinement rule would need.
sequencing: Ride-along under strategy rule 4: it extends the in-house error-estimation work on ladders the lab already owns. Subordinate to the Ladder V queue under rule 1.
gate: STRATEGY PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim: 'Convergence & error estimation: Roache/Eca-Hoekstra already in house -> extend: goal-oriented (adjoint-weighted) error estimates as a mission primitive -- the numerics flex almost nobody ships.' Operationalised in three parts, all required. (a) A prototype estimate on the geometric flat-plate ladder, graded against the refinement channel's own answer on the rungs where that channel earns a band, with the agreement reported as a number and a disagreement treated as a defect in the prototype until proven otherwise. (b) A demonstration on the transonic wing rung whose adjoint gradient is verified against finite differences, reporting the estimated discretization error in the objective and the per-cell contribution map. (c) The primitive lands with the same refusal discipline the existing channel has, returning nothing rather than a number when its own admissibility conditions are unmet, and stating those conditions. An estimate that never refuses fails part (c) by construction.
